title: Fleet steering message (principal <-> director <-> dispatcher <-> executors)
description: The message contract for the session fleet operating model (M26, issue #160; role vocabulary declared by issue #777). The principal orders the director, the director is the only sender of directives to the dispatcher, the dispatcher only spawns epic-focused executors per a directive, and executors report results back through the dispatcher. Everything else is refused. The role vocabulary is the closed set in governance/vocabulary/fleet.yaml.

schema.description: Envelope version (issue #777). Absent means 1: the field is additive, exactly as `nonce` was in issue #161, so every message that predates it stays valid. Schema 2 is the current dialect and emits the current role names ONLY — a retired role in a schema-2 envelope is refused by `channel.validate`, by name. The distinction matters because it is the state ADR-0012 warns about: two vocabularies both quietly authoritative. The single authority for the vocabulary is governance/vocabulary/fleet.yaml.

id.description: Unique message id (uuid4). Stamped by the channel when absent.

from.description: Sender role. Both dialects are accepted on READ (dual-accept): schema 2 spells the four roles principal/director/dispatcher/executor-<name>, schema 1 spelled them operator/brain/sister/subagent-<name>. A schema-2 envelope may not carry a schema-1 role.

to.description: Recipient role, in either declared dialect. principal -> director (orders), director -> dispatcher (directives), up-only for reports and escalations.

type.description: directive = brain order; ack/result = sister/subagent reports; halt = stop signal.

ts.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp; stamped by the channel when absent.

runtime.description: The SENDER's runtime id (issue #1273, parent #1268), from the closed vocabulary fleet/runtimes.yaml declares. Optional on read (a message with no runtime is judged only on role/hierarchy, as before), but once present it is checked against `control-plane/control/verbs.yaml::allowed_runtimes` (task.verb), `integrations/paperclip/adapters/skills` (task.skill) and `integrations/paperclip/adapters/secrets` (task.secret) allowlists by `fleet/channel.py::validate`. A verb/skill/secret outside the sender runtime's list is refused by name (verb-not-allowed:<runtime>:<verb> / skill-not-allowed:<runtime>:<skill> / secret-not-allowed:<runtime>:<secret>).

on_behalf_of.description: Cross-session permission laundering guard: the runtime this directive's action is REALLY being carried out for (e.g. a denied deepseek-executor asking a permitted runtime to run the same verb for it). When present, the ORIGINATING runtime's allowlist is checked in addition to the sender's — a denial on either side refuses the whole directive as laundering:<on_behalf_of>:<verb>.

correlation_id.description: Binds a result/ack to the directive that caused it.

nonce.description: Anti-replay token for a directive (issue #161). Stamped by the channel when absent; send refuses a nonce already seen in the sent, inbox or done mailbox. The rest of the envelope stays v1 — the field is additive.

control.description: Brain-only control action for the sister loop: poke | refresh | halt.

model.description: FinOps block: the model tier and thinking effort the target must run at. The vocabulary is the harvested one (governance/finops/policy.json, issue #164): tiers from capital-underwriting config/leaderboard/tier-policy.json, thinking effort from leaderboard lib/fleet-roster.sh role_effort(). A subagent may not choose its own tier, and an override is refused by governance/finops/chooser.py.

budget_hint.description: Optional cost hint for the subagent's run.

task.description: Work to execute: an issue (and optionally the epic it serves). An order may instead carry a non-work kind, which the brain answers without dispatching anything.

kind.description: work (default) needs an issue; status/report/ping are answered by the brain without dispatching to the sister.

verb.description: A control-plane verb (control-plane/control/verbs.yaml id) this directive invokes. Checked against the sender runtime's (and, if on_behalf_of is set, the originating runtime's) allowed_runtimes at spawn/dispatch (issue #1273).

skill.description: A skill id (integrations/paperclip/adapters/skills registry) this directive loads. Checked against the sender runtime's allowlist (issue #1273).

secret.description: A secret's gsm_path (integrations/paperclip/adapters/secrets catalog) this directive reads. Checked against the sender runtime's allowlist (issue #1273); never the secret's value (GR-6).

title.description: Optional title, used by the brain's FinOps floor check (a security/auth/IaC order never dispatches at flash/none).

files.description: The files this lane owns (issue #718). The capacity gate (fleet/capacity.py) uses it to hold a directive whose file set intersects an in-flight lane's — AO-GR-24: a wave is provably file-disjoint before dispatch. Additive: a directive that declares no files is ADMITTED, and the gate reports it as unattributable by name, so an undeclared lane is never silently called disjoint. An operator who would rather hold undeclared work sets AO_LANE_FILES_REQUIRED=1.
